verdict.rationale: Bitwarden's own docs give a procedure to install and deploy Bitwarden on your own Linux server, and the Public API docs refer to a self-hosted deployment URL, so the core self-hosting capability is first-party. The pack does not document that every secret stays inside the perimeter, so the second half of the story is unproven and full credit is not warranted. missing for 10: documentation that a self-hosted instance keeps all vault data and secrets on-premises with no external dependency (e.g. cloud licensing or relay services), deployment depth beyond a single Linux install line, and independent hands-on corroboration of a self-hosted sync server.

support.subject: As an IT admin, I can self-host the sync server on my own infrastructure and keep every secret inside my perimeter

citations.quote: This article will walk you through the procedure to install and deploy Bitwarden to your own Linux server.
